text:
The presidential pardon power was intended to be an instrument of justice and mercy. NOT a way for wealthy donors, political allies, and well-connected criminals to buy their way out of accountability.
 
The American justice system should not operate on a pay-to-play basis, where the wealthy and politically connected get special treatment while ordinary Americans are held to a different standard.
 
That's why today, alongside Rep. Jason Crow, I introduced the Abuse of the Pardon Prevention Act to crack down on potential corruption and conflicts of interest in the presidential pardon process.
 
Our legislation would strengthen independent oversight of presidential pardons, establish safeguards against bribery, require greater transparency around financial conflicts of interest, and prohibit presidents from pardoning themselves.
 
This isn't about Democrats or Republicans. It's about ensuring that NO president, regardless of political party, can abuse the pardon power for personal or political gain.
 
The Constitution provides the president with extraordinary authority to grant clemency. Americans deserve to know how that authority is being used, who’s benefiting, and why.
 
We need accountability. We need transparency. And we need to put an end to the pardon industrial complex.
